1.mascotDialogue: Once the expression becomes a tree, evaluating her is simple — solve both children, then apply the operator at the parent. No precedence table needed at evaluation time — the shape, she already knows the order.

2.mascotDialogue: Line 8, the base case — a leaf, she simply returns her digit. Lines 9 and 10 recurse into both children before line 11 combines them. The bottom of the tree, she evaluates first, always.

3.mascotDialogue: Because plus sits underneath times, she is forced to resolve first — this is precedence, shown as depth in the tree, instead of a rule you must memorize.

4.mascotDialogue: This bug hides well, precisely because multiplication does not care about order. Swap the operator to subtraction in your head, and this exact same shape starts lying to you.
